title: Branching scenario
description: A story where each choice leads to a different scene and ending. Learners can step back and try other paths; the ending reached sets the score.
demoHtml:
You arrive for your shift. The table saw's blade guard is off, and a coworker says, "Just one quick cut, it's fine."

  • Make the cut carefully
  • Refit the guard first
  • Ask the supervisor

The board kicks back and hits the wall beside you. Nobody is hurt.

  • Keep going, it was a fluke
  • Shut the saw down and report it

You find the guard, but one mounting screw is missing.

  • Use it, it mostly holds
  • Tag the saw out of service

Your supervisor thanks you and asks you to tag the saw out of service.

  • Tag it and log it

Your supervisor tags the saw out and asks what happened.

  • Explain what you did

Best outcome. The saw is tagged out and logged before anyone uses it.

The guard shifted during the next cut. A guard with missing hardware is the same as no guard.

Reporting it was right. The kickback was the warning you didn't need to get.

A second kickback breaks your thumb. Near misses are the cheapest lesson the shop offers.
